sources.name: MaineDOT Crash Locations - 10 Years Complete (ArcGIS Online item b8dd5e49520d4b7495ad8aa3e547b255, owner MaineDOT.IT; the Maine Public Crash Query Tool's data)
sources.access: open (ArcGIS REST, no login; refreshed weekly)
sources.licence_quote: Users must assume responsibility in determining the usability of this data for their purposes. (item licenseInfo, MEGIS disclaimer)
sources.street_names_note: no street names: PRIMARY_ROUTE_NAME is a route code (US 302, ST RTE 26, INT 295 SB) or a road-inventory id (RD INV 05 60621; 38.4% of Cumberland 2024); no cross street; NODE_ID / ELEMENT_ID / route milepoint given
sources.keys_linkable: no: unit and person tables aren't published; CRASH_ID and REPORT_NUMBER on the crash row; driver actions of units 1-2 flattened onto it

placement_sample.note: every crash has a MaineDOT Route Log Mile point inside Maine; the layer has no street names, so the hidden-GPS locator test can't run (nothing to locate from), and there are no no-GPS crashes to rescue (4 of 359,187 statewide)

blockers: licence for paid use not granted (MEGIS disclaimer only)
no crash unit costs or statewide rates in MaineDOT's published manuals
no street names, units or persons in the public layer
user_actions: Ask MaineDOT (Office of Safety / MEGIS) for written OK to show this layer in a paid product
Decide whether Maine studies may use USDOT BCA Guidance crash costs (MaineDOT's own grant BCAs use them)
Optional: MaineDOT ADVANCED USER access to the Public Crash Query Tool (needs sign-up and approval) for unit/person detail

cities.licence: not checked; derived from MaineDOT data, so the state layer is used
